contract: Validated canonical append/replay and conservative Store confirmation boundary, owning Writer shell and volatile Memory test double. Selected supplied-decision count_step laws only; no storage engine or delivery guarantee.
limits: Memory is volatile. No disk/fsync/replication, WAL, lease, tamper evidence or exactly-once claim.
L1a–L5 cover count_step with supplied decisions only, not classify, refold equivalence, reducers, the Elixir shell or providers.
Absence never proves non-commit; indeterminate writes stop the Writer. Unknown reconciliation requires deliberate fresh-nonce CAS or read-only inspection.
Revisions/sequences are nonnegative signed-bigint values; versions/positions are positive signed-integer values; stored text is UTF-8 without NUL.
Checkpoint support is optional and requires state/checkpoint; no checkpoint dependency is needed for replay, Store, Memory or ordinary Writer use.

Store-only reason :caller_transaction (ELZ-032, same ID): the shell accepts the Store reply {:rejected, :caller_transaction} and the read error :caller_transaction, and confirm/5 returns {:unknown, :caller_transaction}. A third-party Store returning that reply was classed indeterminate before and is rejected now. The ID is kept because the change is strictly additive: the shell already trusts Store-only rejection reasons (:torn_repair_unsupported, :unfenced_tail), the value adds no new trust relationship, it is the only way to restore the integration/sql Contract without returning indeterminate, Memory never produces it, and no in-repo consumer matches the reasons exhaustively.

grounding.claim: L1a: duplicate_keeps_total, quantified supplied-decision count_step law only; no classify, shell or provider proof.
L1b: duplicate_keeps_cursor, quantified supplied-decision count_step law only; no classify, shell or provider proof.
L2: out_of_order_keeps_total, quantified supplied-decision count_step law only; no classify, shell or provider proof.
L3: out_of_order_keeps_applied, quantified supplied-decision count_step law only; no classify, shell or provider proof.
L4: gap_marks_damaged, quantified supplied-decision count_step law only; no classify, shell or provider proof.
L5: non_state_bearing_keeps_total, quantified supplied-decision count_step law only; no classify, shell or provider proof.
Pinned Cure compiles/audits the production source. The false gap law and duplicate-track mutation are rejected in bundled tests; these controls bound the selected supplied-decision proof scope.
Finite D1–D6/D18 replay, seed/truncation, reducer failure and validation scenarios; selected-law compilation and both negative controls, not universal recovery proofs.
Volatile CAS, uncertainty/readback and staged-tail fault scenarios.
Owning init, uniform damaged-seed refusal, conflict, indeterminate shutdown and post-commit failure scenarios.
Core and Memory share the portable numeric/text domain; malformed/rejected cases.
K1–K11 against volatile Memory; named checks, error and missing-hook cases, not disk persistence.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler/kernel for selected equality laws and the replay ABI.
Elixir validation, exceptions and BEAM execution are upstream contracts, not proved here.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer, process lifecycle and crypto APIs are upstream contracts; no disk durability or exactly-once guarantee.
Consumer reducers are pure/deterministic; folds, codecs and limits are supplied by the consumer. Store CAS arbitrates revision writes, not business ownership or intent.

telemetry.contract: Damaged/torn states are returned values; no telemetry events emitted.

config.contract: Start-time store, stream, fold specification and limits; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: Writer supplies OTP start/stop only; no business pause/drain/resume contract.
